Home / 3D Scale Visualizer

Direct answer

See the scale difference before you print

The visualizer compares miniature scales against a calibrated 10mm grid so you can judge how a 28mm, 32mm, 35mm or ratio-scale model will look next to figures you already own. It uses the same eye-level baselines as the conversion chart, and it runs entirely in your browser.

Questions this tool answers

How does the 3D scale visualizer work?

It places a calibrated 10mm grid beside figures scaled with the same eye-level baselines used across STLACCESS, so you can compare 28mm, 32mm, 35mm and ratio scales side by side before you print. Everything runs locally in your browser.

Which miniature scales can I compare?

The visualizer covers 28mm, 32mm, 35mm and 40mm gaming scales plus ratio scales such as 1:35, 1:48, 1:56 and 1:72. The same baselines drive the conversion chart and the slicer percentages in the scale converter.

Why compare by eye level instead of total height?

Gaming labels describe the height of a 175cm human's eyes, which sit at 160cm, while ratio labels are defined from full height. Mixing the two conventions produces models that look visibly wrong, so every comparison here uses eye-level equivalents.
